instantiated_cells.justification: Section 13.66 prohibits lobbying without a license under §13.63, and §13.63(1)(a) sets out the license application procedure for lobbyists.
The statute states a lobbyist license "shall expire on December 31 of each even-numbered year," meaning a 24-month (biennial) renewal cycle.
Section 13.64(1) requires every principal who makes lobbying expenditures exceeding $500 in a calendar year to file a registration statement within 10 days after exceeding $500.

Lobbyists are licensed under §13.63, principals (clients) register under §13.64, and §13.65 requires a separate written authorization for each principal a lobbyist represents — establishing distinct registration regimes for lobbyists and their clients.

Section 13.63(1)(a) enumerates the application requirements (signature, social security number, fee) and does not require submission of a photograph; no other section in the subchapter imposes such a requirement.
Section 13.621(3) exempts elective state officials, local officials, tribal officials, and legislative employees from §§13.63, 13.64, 13.65, 13.68, and 13.695 when acting in an official capacity.

Section 13.621(2) provides that an agency filing a statement under §13.695 and its named officials are not subject to §§13.625, 13.63, 13.64, 13.65, or 13.68 except as provided in §13.695, i.e., a partial exemption substituting agency-specific disclosure.

unscoreable_emissions.reason: Section 13.64(3) requires principals to provide written notice of new general areas/agencies before attempting to influence action in them, but specifies no fixed number of days for amending registration; §13.695(2) sets a 10-day amendment deadline but only for state agency statements, not lobbyist registrations. No numeric amendment deadline for lobbyist/principal registrations appears in the bundled text.
